reason: The checker question is 'what is the base type (string / number / bigint / other) of each `+` operand, with literal types widened and unions required to agree?'. The port classifies operands only when they are literals (number, string or template, `123n` / `BigInt()`, array, object). Secondary: error-tolerant-parse. Both fixtures contain a syntax error TypeScript recovers from, so the harness sees 0 findings. On copies with only those errors fixed (probed off-harness), the port finds 14/25 with 0 FP. Every remaining miss has an identifier or property-access operand whose type comes from a declaration. Checker APIs: getTypeAtLocation of each operand, typeToString, string/number/bigint/enum flags (:76-107). Line 27 needs initializer inference, line 31 an alias's member type.
